newsitem.title: UK: Foreign investors head for door in Czech battle.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors head for door in Czech battle.

text.p: Foreign investors are seeking to exit Czech equity and fixed-income positions following Czech National Bank (CNB) moves to prop up the ailing crown, analysts said on Thursday.
"In the short term (foreign) investors are caught between the devil and the deep blue sea," said James Oates, a director of eastern and central European equities at Union Bank of Switzerland.
The CNB, locked in a battle with currency speculators, has pushed up the one-week repo rate to 75 percent and choked off money market liquidity.

"There has been a lot of concern over the last several months about the long-term direction of policy in the Czech Republic," Oates said, adding that this week's events will only serve to further sour investor sentiment.

"Either the Czech Crown devalues and so their investment falls by that amount or it doesn't devalue but interest rates stay very high and the performance of their equity holdings is likely to be very poor," Oates said.
"There is no reason for (foreign investors) to stay in the Czech Republic, in fact they are trying to bail out as fast as possible," he said.
If rates remain high, Czech bonds will look good in comparison to equities, according to David Mars, an analyst at SBC Warburg, but uncertainty remains high and the market will be illiquid.
"That's what we mean by emerging markets -- you can buy them but in an emergency you can't sell them," Mars said.

But analysts said that there is relatively little foreign investment in Czech equities and bonds. "There has been a steady disillusionment over the past 18 months, mainly with poor market regulation and corporate governance.
"It's now mostly currency speculation," an analyst said.
Recent events may have far-reaching effects in emerging markets, analysts said.

Mars ties the Czech crisis, and last week's run on the Thai baht, to uncertainty over U.S. interest rate direction, "The international risk premium has risen dramatically in the last few days because of the Fed."
With returns in emerging markets down as compared to recent years, investors are withdrawing support from what they see to be the weakest markets, according to Mars.
